page: Microsoft Azure E16_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The server provisions 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It comes with 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. No discrete graphics processors are included, and the instance does not feature bundled local storage, requiring external networked block storage for persistent data volumes.

Hardware instruction set extensions on this host include AVX-512 (Foundation and VNNI), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, which aid vector calculations and cryptographic tasks. In standardized performance benchmarks, the E16_v5 largely registers within the average tier across general compute and memory evaluations. It scored 1635.0 in single-core and 9891.0 in multi-core Geekbench assessments, paired with a PassMark CPU score of 21149.34. Memory throughput reaches 97.3 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 53.92 GB/sec for uncached writes, while cached 16 KB read throughput clocks at 833.81 GB/sec. In synthetic in-memory workloads, it achieved 15.85 million Redis SET operations per second and 8005.49 in PassMark database operations.

Machine learning CPU inference demonstrates strong results for small models, achieving 279.0 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter architecture. For medium-sized 7B parameter models, performance aligns with standard CPU baselines at 35.06 prompt tokens per second and 12.21 generation tokens per second. The primary hardware tradeoff of this instance configuration is the total absence of integrated local NVMe storage, meaning all I/O is reliant on networked disk options. Because of its 1:8 core-to-memory allocation, the E16_v5 presents an effective resource balance for memory-bound applications, large relational and NoSQL databases, in-memory caching tiers, and enterprise-grade backend services.
description: Microsoft Azure E16_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C x86_64 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. It delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores and provides 128.0 GB of RAM, adhering to an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration features 48 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions. It contains zero GPUs and provides no integrated local storage, requiring remote storage solutions for operational disk requirements. Standardized testing highlights balanced metrics, including 15.85 million Redis SET operations per second, 97.3 GB/sec large-block read memory bandwidth, and 279.0 tokens per second for small-model LLM text generation. The E16_v5 is designed for memory-intensive workloads, including distributed in-memory caches, enterprise databases, and data processing tasks requiring substantial RAM overhead.
